questions.q: Which concept removes duplicates and fixes missing values?
questions.why: Bad data gives bad models - cleaning removes duplicates, fixes errors and fills or drops missing values.
questions.example: Two rows for the same customer, and an age of "-5": both get fixed before training.
questions.say: Bad data gives bad models. Cleaning removes duplicates, fixes errors, and handles missing values.

questions.q: Which concept creates informative inputs such as lags and rolling statistics?
questions.why: Turning raw data into informative inputs often helps a model more than choosing a fancier algorithm.
questions.example: From daily sales, create "sales last week" and "7-day average" as new columns.
questions.say: Turning raw data into useful inputs, like last week's sales or a seven day average, often helps more than a fancier model.

questions.q: Which concept happens when a model memorises its training data and fails on new data?
questions.why: The model memorises noise in the training data instead of the real pattern, so it fails on new data.
questions.example: A student who memorised last year's answers but can't solve a new question.
questions.say: The model memorises its training data instead of the real pattern, like a student who memorised old answers and fails a new exam.

questions.q: Which concept repeats train and validation splits to estimate how well a model generalises?
questions.why: The data is split into folds; each fold takes a turn as the test set, giving a more reliable score.
questions.example: 5-fold CV trains 5 times and averages the 5 scores.
questions.say: The data is split into folds, and each fold takes a turn as the test set. Averaging the scores gives a more reliable estimate.

questions.q: Which model is an ensemble of decision trees built with bagging?
questions.why: Many decision trees are trained on random samples of the data, and their votes are combined.
questions.example: Asking 100 slightly different experts and going with the majority.
questions.say: Many decision trees each learn from a random sample of the data, and their votes are combined. Like asking a hundred experts.

questions.q: Which concept reduces dimensions linearly while keeping the maximum variance?
questions.why: PCA finds new axes along which the data varies most and keeps only the top few.
questions.example: 50 correlated measurements squeezed into 2 axes you can plot.
questions.say: It finds the directions in which the data varies most, and keeps only the top few. Many columns become a handful you can plot.

questions.q: Which concept retrieves facts from a knowledge graph before a language model answers?
questions.why: GraphRAG retrieves connected facts from a knowledge graph, so the answer can follow relationships.
questions.example: "Which tools does project X use?" follows edges  project -> uses -> tool.
questions.say: It retrieves connected facts from a knowledge graph, so the answer can follow relationships between things.

questions.q: Which tool runs open language models locally through a simple API?
questions.why: Ollama downloads and runs open models on your own machine behind a simple local API.
questions.example: ollama run llama3.2 - a chat model running offline on your laptop.
questions.say: It downloads open models and runs them on your own computer, behind a simple local A P I.

questions.q: Which concept shows why a model made a certain prediction?
questions.why: Explainability methods show which inputs drove a prediction, so people can trust and check the model.
questions.example: "Loan denied mainly because of: low income, short credit history."
questions.say: It shows which inputs drove a prediction, so people can check and trust the model.

questions.q: Which concept tracks data drift and performance after deployment?
questions.why: After deployment, real-world data drifts away from the training data, so performance must be watched.
questions.example: A sales model trained before a pandemic slowly gets worse - monitoring raises an alarm.
questions.say: After deployment, real data slowly drifts away from the training data. Monitoring notices when performance drops.
